sections.h2: Where is Pearl, Mississippi, and what kind of city is it?
sections.html:
Pearl is a city in Rankin County that sits on the east bank of the Pearl River, directly across from Jackson. It is the most populous city in Rankin County and part of the Jackson metro area, with 27,115 residents at the 2020 census.

The city covers about 25.6 square miles and borders Flowood, Brandon, Richland and Jackson. Its main commercial street is U.S. Highway 80, and Interstate 20, Interstate 55, U.S. 49 and Mississippi Highway 25 (Lakeland Drive) all serve the area. Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport is in Rankin County too.

For a seller, the practical point is that Pearl is a suburb with its own city hall, police, fire department and school district, even though most people think of it as part of greater Jackson. That means permits, code questions and school boundaries run through Pearl, while the property tax bill is handled by Rankin County.

sections.h2: A short history of Pearl and why it matters to homeowners
sections.html:
Pearl was incorporated late. Residents voted on incorporation in 1968, the name was picked in January 1969, and the Mississippi Supreme Court ordered the city's incorporation on June 5, 1973, with the charter presented on June 29, 1973.

Before that the area was a railroad and school community called Pearson, then Pearl, with a one-room school petitioned for in 1911. Suburban growth out of Jackson in the 1960s drove most of the housing stock. The Pearl Municipal Separate School District was created by city ordinance in 1976.

Pearl grew largely through suburban development out of Jackson, so sellers here often hold houses with systems that have aged. When a roof or foundation problem makes a house hard to finance, a cash buyer who takes the property as is becomes a practical option.

sections.h2: What does Pearl's economy look like for people trying to sell?
sections.html:
Pearl's economy mixes retail, hospitality, manufacturing, education and government work. Data USA reported health care and social assistance, retail trade and educational services as the three largest employment sectors in 2024.

The same source listed a 2024 median household income of $61,695 and a median property value of $182,500. Those are citywide medians, so a three-bedroom ranch near Old Brandon Road and a house with deferred repairs will not sit at the same number.

  • Outlets of Mississippi is a 315,000 square foot outlet center in the city.
  • West Rankin Industrial Park is the city's main industrial area. In 2026 Siemens Energy announced a new grid-component plant there, with the Mississippi Development Authority citing an investment of up to $300 million and up to 300 jobs.
  • The West Rankin Parkway opened in November 2025, linking Highway 80 in Pearl to Flowood Drive in Flowood.
  • Trustmark Park hosts the Mississippi Mud Monsters of the Frontier League, which began play there in 2025.

New employers and road links can help neighborhood demand over time, but they do not fix a house that needs work today. Sellers should not count on future projects to carry a listing.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled on a Pearl house?
sections.html:
Rankin County values and bills the property, and the tax is due by February 1 for the preceding assessment year. If February 1 lands on a weekend or holiday, payment the following Monday carries no penalty or interest.

Under the Mississippi Constitution a single-family, owner-occupied home is Class I and assessed at 10 percent of true value. Other real estate, including a rental house or an inherited home no one lives in, is Class II at 15 percent. The bill is true value times the assessment ratio times the combined millage of the county, city and school district. Assessors must revalue real property at least every four years.

The Rankin County Tax Collector mails statements by December and accepts payment at (601) 825-1467 or through the county's online payment page. The Chancery Clerk's office notes that unpaid property goes to a tax sale in August, and the owner has two years from the sale date to redeem before it matures to the buyer or the State.

If you are behind on taxes, the amount has to be cleared before a clean title can pass, so ask the Tax Collector for a payoff figure early.

sections.h2: Does homestead exemption change when I sell a house in Pearl?
sections.html:
Yes, because the exemption follows who lives in the home on January 1. To claim it, a buyer must own and occupy the house as a primary residence on January 1 of the tax year, and the deed must be filed with the Chancery Clerk before January 7.

The regular tier gives a credit of up to $300 for owners under 65. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, are exempt on the first $7,500 of assessed value, and some veterans and surviving spouses qualify for a full exemption. Applications go to the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1.

A buyer who closes in the spring should know that, under that rule, the exemption for that year probably will not be available to them, and an investor who buys a house to rent never qualifies. A home sold by an owner who had the exemption may also need a fresh application from the next owner. Sorting this out at the closing table avoids a surprise on the following tax bill.

sections.h2: What Mississippi law requires a Pearl seller to disclose
sections.html:
Mississippi requires most sellers to give the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. Under Section 89-1-503, it must be delivered as soon as practicable before title transfers, and the seller notes compliance on the contract or an addendum.

If the statement arrives after the buyer has already made an offer, the buyer has three days after hand delivery, or five days after mailing, to cancel the offer in writing. If a seller skips or only partly completes the form, the buyer is presumed to be on notice to ask about the missing items, and licensed agents are not disciplined for the omission.

  • Fill in the form honestly, including known roof leaks, foundation movement and past water damage.
  • Keep receipts for repairs, since they answer most buyer questions.
  • Hand over the statement with the first offer rather than later, so no one gets a cancellation window.

A cash buyer who purchases as is still receives the disclosure. The difference is that the buyer is pricing in the repairs instead of asking you to make them.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling fast in Pearl?
sections.html:
A Pearl seller can list with an agent, sell directly to an investor for cash, or fix the house first and then list. The best choice depends on the house's condition and how soon you need to close.

  • Listing suits a house in good shape and a seller who can wait through showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval.
  • A direct cash sale suits houses with repair needs, tax or probate pressure, or tenants and moves on a deadline.
  • Repair-then-list can work if the repairs are cosmetic and cheap, but costs add up and take time to finish.

Before any sale, a title search will show liens, unpaid taxes and whether the seller holds legal title. The Rankin County Chancery Clerk notes that a deed needs a notarized seller signature, a legal description with indexing instructions, and names, addresses and phone numbers for sellers, buyers and the preparer. Only an attorney or title company can search the records and draft the deed. If any permit work was left open on the house, the City of Pearl's Community Development office on Old Brandon Road is the place to ask.

Cash Home Buyers works with Pearl sellers who want a straightforward as-is sale, and we explain what we can and cannot offer up front.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Pearl, MS?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A cash sale can close as soon as the title work is ready, while a traditional listing has to wait for showings, a buyer's loan and appraisal. Title problems and unpaid taxes slow either path.

faqs.q: Do I need to make repairs before selling in Pearl?
faqs.a: No. Mississippi does not require repairs before a sale, but you do have to complete the written property condition disclosure statement. Buyers who purchase as is typically price the repairs in.

faqs.q: When are Rankin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by February 1 for property assessed the preceding year. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, you have until the following Monday without penalty.
The Pearl Public School District serves the city. Its schools include Pearl High School, Pearl Junior High, Pearl Upper Elementary, Pearl Lower Elementary and Northside Elementary.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when a Pearl house sells?
faqs.a: The Rankin County Chancery Clerk records deeds. The deed needs a notarized seller signature and a legal description, and a title company or attorney normally prepares it.
